title: How to Brief a YouTube Thumbnail Designer
h1: How to brief a YouTube thumbnail designer
description: Brief a thumbnail designer: your channel style, video topic, text, faces and images, sizes, testing, revisions and what makes a thumbnail easy to read.
intro: A thumbnail is the small picture people see before they decide to watch a video. It works together with the title to promise something worth clicking. A designer can make thumbnails that look professional and consistent, but only if they understand your channel and each video. This article explains what to include in a brief and how to judge thumbnails fairly.

faq.q: What size should a thumbnail be?
faq.a: The standard is a widescreen image, 1280 by 720 pixels. Ask the designer to follow the current platform guidance.

faq.q: Should I put text on it?
faq.a: Short text can help, but it must be readable at a small size. Three or four large words is a common limit.

faq.q: Do I need to be in the thumbnail?
faq.a: Not necessarily. Faces help many channels, but some topics work better with objects or graphics.

faq.q: How many thumbnails should I order?
faq.a: Start with one or two to test the style. If it works, order a batch for consistency.
Yes. Many creators compare two designs for the same video and keep the one that gets more clicks.
